calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 25% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Utah couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Utah usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.3% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.7% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Toronto’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Toronto has a better power play than most. Even by those standards, this was a big night: 16.7 expected goals per 60 on the power play, against their usual 7.8 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: Utah hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Utah is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 65 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 117 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: The Mammoth squeak past the Maple Leafs
paras: Daniil But opened the scoring for the Mammoth late in the first. The second period brought six goals. Vincent Trocheck and Mikhail Sergachev scored just over three minutes apart early in the period to stretch the lead to 3-0. Auston Matthews got the Maple Leafs on the board on the power play a little over a minute later. Dylan Guenther stretched the lead to 4-1 late in the second, but Jack Roslovic cut Utah’s lead to 4-2 a little over two minutes later. MacKenzie Weegar made it 5-2 for the Mammoth just under three minutes later, and that goal turned out to be the winner. John Tavares and Gavin McKenna scored less than four minutes apart midway through the third to make it 5-4, but the Mammoth held on.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves for the Mammoth, and Anthony Stolarz allowed five goals on 28 shots.
Guenther took three penalties on his own. The Mammoth moved to 5-2-0, and the Maple Leafs fell to 3-3-1.

items.text: Auston Matthews has a point in five straight games.
